1.title: Switching: VLANs, Spanning Tree and MTU
1.text: Welcome to Module nine: Switching: V L A Ns, Spanning Tree and M T U. It covers the exam area two point zero Network Implementation. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. two point two Given a scenario, configure switching technologies and features: V L A N, V L A N database, switch virtual interface (S V I). Interface configuration (native V L A N, voice V L A N, eight oh two dot one Q tagging, link aggregation, speed, duplex). Spanning tree. Maximum transmission unit (M T U) and jumbo frames. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: two point zero Network Implementation (twenty percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: VLANs
1.text: V L A Ns. A virtual L A N (V L A N) splits one physical switch into several logical networks (broadcast domains). Devices in different V L A Ns need a router or a layer three switch to talk. V L A N database. The switch's list of V L A N I D s and names (I D s one to four thousand ninety-four). Access port. Carries one V L A N, untagged, to an end device. Trunk port. Carries several V L A Ns between switches, using eight oh two dot one Q tags. eight oh two dot one Q tagging. Adds a four-byte tag with the V L A N I D to frames on a trunk. Native V L A N. The V L A N whose frames cross a trunk untagged; must match on both ends.

1.title: VLANs, continued
1.text: V L A Ns. Voice V L A N. A separate V L A N for I P phones so voice gets its own segment and Qo S. S V I (switch virtual interface). A layer three interface for a V L A N on a layer three switch; acts as the V L A N's default gateway.

1.title: VLANs, continued
1.text: V L A Ns. The figure shows this: A trunk carrying V L A Ns ten and twenty between two switches, with access ports and an S V I. Exam tip: A native V L A N mismatch causes errors and leaks. Inter-V L A N routing needs an S V I or a router subinterface.

1.title: Interface settings
1.text: Interface settings. Speed. ten or one hundred or one thousand megabits per second or more; both ends should agree (auto-negotiation). Duplex. Full duplex (send and receive together) or half; a mismatch causes collisions, slow speed and errors. Link aggregation. Bundles several physical links into one logical link for more bandwidth and redundancy, using L A C P (I E E E eight oh two dot three A D).

1.title: Spanning tree
1.text: Spanning tree. Spanning Tree Protocol (S T P) prevents layer two loops in networks with redundant links by blocking some paths. Root bridge. The reference switch chosen by the lowest bridge I D (priority, then M A C address). Root port. Each non-root switch's best path to the root. Designated port. Forwarding port for a segment. Blocking or alternate port. Blocked to break the loop. States (classic). Blocking, listening, learning, forwarding. R S T P (rapid S T P, eight oh two dot one W). Converges in seconds instead of tens of seconds.

1.title: Spanning tree, continued
1.text: Spanning tree. The figure shows this: A triangle of switches with the root bridge, forwarding links and one blocked link. Exam tip: The root bridge is the switch with the lowest priority; ties go to the lowest M A C address. Without S T P a broadcast storm can bring down the network.

1.title: MTU and jumbo frames
1.text: M T U and jumbo frames. The maximum transmission unit (M T U) is the largest frame payload an interface sends: one thousand five hundred bytes for standard Ethernet. Jumbo frames (about nine thousand bytes) cut overhead for storage and data center traffic but every device on the path must support them. Exam tip: Trunk ports carry tagged V L A Ns; access ports carry one untagged V L A N. A native V L A N mismatch causes problems.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Two switches must carry traffic for several V L A Ns over one link. What should be configured? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: An eight oh two dot one Q trunk. Trunks carry multiple tagged V L A Ns.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. V L A N ten and V L A N twenty hosts cannot communicate. What is needed? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A router or layer three switch with S V Is. Different V L A Ns need layer three routing.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A redundant triangle of switches suffers a broadcast storm. Which protocol should prevent this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Spanning Tree Protocol. S T P blocks redundant paths to prevent loops.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which switch becomes the spanning tree root bridge by default? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The switch with the lowest bridge priority, then lowest M A C address. The lowest bridge I D wins.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Four one gigabit per second links must act as one logical link for bandwidth and redundancy. Which feature fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Link aggregation with L A C P. L A C P bundles links into one logical link.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which setting keeps I P phone traffic on its own segment? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A voice V L A N. A voice V L A N separates phone traffic.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does eight oh two dot one Q do? Answer: Adds a V L A N tag to frames on a trunk. Question two. What is the standard Ethernet M T U? Answer: one thousand five hundred bytes. Question three. What does an S V I provide? Answer: A layer three interface for a V L A N (its default gateway).

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What protocol aggregates links? Answer: L A C P. Question five. What does R S T P improve? Answer: Convergence speed. Question six. What happens to native V L A N traffic on a trunk? Answer: It crosses untagged.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. V L A N: I D s one to four thousand ninety-four; access versus trunk; eight oh two dot one Q; native V L A N untagged; voice V L A N; S V I. Interface: speed and duplex must match; L A C P link aggregation. S T P: root bridge (lowest I D), root, designated, blocked; R S T P faster. M T U: one thousand five hundred standard; jumbo about nine thousand, support end to end.
